pages.title: My dog Max and a kitten called Luna · 1/3
paragraphs: My name is Diego, and I live in **San Antonio**. I have a dog. His name is Max. He is three years old, and he is brown and white. “**So adorable**!” people say when they see him.

Last Saturday we went to the park. A woman said, “Look! What a cute dog!” “Thanks,” I said. “His name is Max.” She asked, “**How old is he?**” “He’s three years old,” I answered. “Does he like people?” she asked. “Yes, he loves people,” I said.
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: My dog Max and a kitten called Luna · 2/3
paragraphs: The woman has a cat called Luna. “**Aww**!” I said when I saw her photo. Luna is small and gray, and she sleeps all day. A **cat nap** is perfect for her! My grandmother says, “**Curiosity killed the cat**,” because Luna opens every box.

In school, I learned a poem called “Three Little Kittens.” An American writer, Eliza Lee Follen, wrote it in 1843. Three kittens lose their mittens, and their mother is not happy. The kittens find the mittens in the end, and everybody is happy again.

pages.title: My dog Max and a kitten called Luna · 3/3
paragraphs: Now Max and Luna are friends. They run in the park, and then they sleep. I love my little pet family.
